latest_census.confidence: high (the repo has already built from it)
latest_census.notes: National Population and Housing Census 2021 (enumerated November 2021; National Report March 2023). Asks caste/ethnicity (142 groups), mother tongue (124 languages, plus second and ancestral language) and religion (10 categories), and publishes all three by province (7), district (77) and local level (753). SOURCES.md 'Nepal: three fields, one census, and a boundary file that does not fit' documents the build from the National Report PDF.

already_in_map: All three fields at 7/7 provinces and 66/75 admin2 from the 2021 census National Report. The 9 empty admin2 shapes are the boundary's fault, not the source's: geoBoundaries CGAZ draws 75 shapes for 77 districts, two names ('Bara', 'Saptari') appear twice, and Karnali's labels are shifted along by one; eleven districts were withheld by the Wikidata point check because their names sit on the wrong ground. The provinces 'Province 1' and 'Province 2' are CGAZ's old names for Koshi and Madhesh and are aliased.

tier_reason: Already built: a census count of all three fields at province and district. A machine-readable copy is recalled on the census portal, and what remains empty is a boundary-file defect rather than a source gap.
recommended_action: Retry censusnepal.cbs.gov.np with a working network for the xlsx tables (same enumeration; a second reading of the same numbers is a useful check on the PDF parse). Fix the 9 empty admin2 shapes on the boundary side -- swap CGAZ's Nepal admin2 for a 77-district layer (OCHA COD-AB or the Survey Department's) and re-run scripts/verify_shapes.py -- rather than hunting for another source. Nothing here supersedes the existing fill.

whether the 2021 census is in IPUMS-I
summary: Nepal is already the best case on the map: the 2021 census asked caste/ethnicity, mother tongue and religion and the NSO publishes all three by province and district, which the repo has read from the National Report PDF into 7 provinces and 66 districts. The nine empty admin2 shapes are geoBoundaries' fault (75 shapes for 77 districts, duplicated and shifted names), so the next step is a better district layer, not a better source. The census portal's Excel tables are the machine-readable copy to retry with a normal network.
